prompt:
Implement `src/VcfArchitectureClient.java` as a dependency-free, single-file Java client that returns the architecture for `fixtures/estate-inventory.json`. `test/TestMain.java` will pass that fixture to `design(String)` and write the returned JSON to `build/architecture.json`.

Produce an architecture, not a prose explanation. The returned JSON object must itself be a greenfield `SddcSpec` valid against the VCF 9.1 installer schema. Design one single-site consolidated VCF 9.1.0.0 management domain on exactly the minimum supported four target hosts, using the supplied reserved hostnames, vSAN with one host failure to tolerate, management and compute resource pools, the required management, vMotion, and vSAN networks, one redundant-uplink distributed switch, and new vCenter, SDDC Manager, and three-node NSX management components.

The source estate contains builds for which the obvious in-place order to VCF 9.1.0.0 is blocked. Route around that incompatibility with a side-by-side target foundation. Add a top-level `migrationPlan` extension conforming to the supplied migration-plan schema. It must cover every inventory component exactly once, preserve its version and build, name its target version and resource, state the replacement or migration action, and name the compatibility and sequencing gates.

Before coding, research current Broadcom-published compatibility, interoperability, and upgrade-path material relevant to these exact source and target combinations. Record the publications consulted under a top-level `research.consulted` array. Each entry must contain a nonblank `title` and the HTTPS Broadcom `url` for that publication.

Keep all implementation in `src/VcfArchitectureClient.java`; do not modify the fixture, `test/TestMain.java`, schemas, compatibility data, license, or verifier. Run `python3 grader/verify.py`.
